authorization: User requested all relevant NT-to-animation cross-RQ analyses, procedure/result documentation, and bold additions to the Results draft.
population: 72 trials from 24 participants: one NT and two animated trials per participant; 16 trials per animation
response_score: S=D=(onset+completion)/2 for animated trials; S=1 if zero retained NT presses during inclusive 0-120 seconds, otherwise S=0; NT D/onset/completion stay missing/inapplicable
tests: 49 two-sided tests: 9 all-trial score gaps; 6 NT score gaps; 5 NT-minus-two-animation-average contrasts; 15 NT-minus-specific-animation contrasts; 4 NT-minus-animated changes in focal score gaps; 3 within-NT Fisher associations; 4 exact participant-permutation same-measure NT/animated associations; 3 ordinal-confidence direction contrasts
aggregation: All-trial participant mean gives each of three trials weight 1/3, hence NT 1/3 and animation 2/3; separate condition contrasts pair each NT only with the same exposed participant's animation; condition-block 50/50 weighting is descriptive sensitivity
gap_tests: Exact sign tests on participant differences; zero differences omitted from the binomial test only; NT binary gaps and binary specific-condition pairs are equivalent to exact McNemar
association_tests: Within NT: Fisher exact independence test; across contexts: exact permutation of binary NT labels against each participant's two-animation mean using doubled average ranks and exact subset-sum enumeration, verified against scipy permutation_test; Q1 associations not estimable because NT Q1 is constant
confidence: Keep original ordinal ratings. NT versus animation uses the mean of the two pairwise NT-minus-animation signs per participant, then an exact sign test. NT Q1-minus-Q2 uses its paired sign; no arithmetic mean of confidence levels
multiplicity: Primary new-extension Holm family of 49; additional expanded Holm family of 79 includes all 30 earlier tests. Report both; no independent replication claim. Earlier package values preserved and labelled by family
bootstrap: Whole participants, preserving within-person trials; percentile pointwise 95%, Bonferroni 99.8979591837% across 49 and 99.9367088608% across 79. Approximate coverage. Associations use frequency-table tie ranks; undefined correlations padded to -1/+1 endpoints and counted
sensitivity: Full-only meaning included in family; 50/50 NT/animation weighting descriptive; delete-one-participant raw and Holm 49 recomputed for every test; expanded 79 deletion correction uses conservative Bonferroni bound 79 times new-test raw p, not unchanged historical deletion p-values
diagnostics: Rebuild from crosswalk, cleaned triggers, questionnaire workbook/scoring key and validated Layer 1 coding; reconcile sanitized questionnaire data and prior animated input, retained presses and exact-120 handling; check population, joins, missingness, score domains, exact binomial and Fisher arithmetic, permutation enumeration, Holm, bootstrap replication, output hashes and source immutability
boundary: Exploratory operational performance under the observed schedule, not common latent ability, task equivalence, intrinsic difficulty, causal effect, stable trait or proof of detecting absence. NT oral success is unchanged-condition recognition; animated M is full-plus-partial intended-meaning interpretation. RQ3 coding remains provisional/single-coder. Gaze, lane distance, latency and event-specific models remain in their existing reports; this extension concerns trigger/recognition/interpretation and relevant confidence links
